Application of urea-based deep eutectic solvent for electrodeposition of copper selenide $\left ( Cu_{2-x}Se/CuSe \right )$ electrocatalyst for hydrogen evolution reaction in acidic medium

abstracts.content: This work presents a simple method for copper selenide electrodeposition on carbon substrate using electrolyte based on a ‘reline’ deep eutectic solvent (choline chloride + urea). A detailed adjustment of the electrodeposition process is presented, including solvent selection, effects of applied potential, duration, and annealing conditions. The materials were characterized using SEM, EDS, XRD, XPS, and Raman. EDS results show that as-synthesized materials contain 60–66 at.% Cu and 34–40 at.% Se, while annealed under optimal conditions (200 °C) exhibit 60–61 at.% Cu. The annealed Cu-Se materials show also morphological changes and crystallinity. XRD of the annealed electrodes indicated the presence of a mixture of $Cu_{2−x}Se$ (cubic $Cu_{1.8}$Se) and hexagonal CuSe phases. The selected materials were tested for $H_{2}$ evolution activity in 0.5 M $H_{2}SO_{4}$, indicating a significant reduction in the HER overpotential of about 120 mV (@10 mA $cm^{−2}$) and 240 mV (@100 mA $cm^{−2}$) compared to carbon substrate. Our work demonstrates also a significant change in the Tafel slope from 169 mV $dec^{−1}$ for the substrate to 43–53 mV $dec^{−1}$ for copper selenide electrodes. This work is the first to highlight the application potential of copper selenide electrodeposited from a DES reline-based electrolyte for the HER in an acidic medium.

results.title: Evolution of microporosity in mature mudstones of the Outer Carpathians, Poland

abstracts.content: The Polish Carpathian region has over 170 years of conventional hydrocarbon exploration history, with numerous discovered oil and gas fields. In recent years, increasing attention has been given to the potential for new, alternative hydrocarbon deposits. This study evaluates three types of mature mudstones from the Oligocene Menilite Beds, Krosno Beds and Grybów Beds, collected from boreholes in the Polish part of the Outer Carpathians, as potential unconventional source and reservoir rocks. X-ray diffraction (XRD), optical and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), N2 adsorption and mercury injection capillary pressure (MICP) techniques were used to evaluate the pore system, organic matter and mineral composition in each lithofacies. The findings reveal that the Menilite Beds mudstone is thermally mature, with Type II/III kerogen. In contrast, the mudstones of the Grybów and Krosno beds are highly thermally mature, corresponding to the dry gas window stage, with kerogen Types IV and mixed III/IV, respectively. All three formations display a fair total organic carbon (TOC) value (0.7%–1.1%) but have low hydrocarbon generation potential (hydrogen index [HI] < 85 mg HC/g TOC). Microscopic observations confirm the presence of both mineral and organic matter pores in all three mature mudstones. Samples are dominated by nanoporosity (average pore size <14 nm), with low effective porosity values across all samples, ranging from 1.51% to 3.59%. Permeability is very low (0.029–0.081 mD). Nitrogen adsorption isotherms are type IV for all mudstones, with H3/H4 hysteresis loops, indicating slit- and wedge-shaped pores. The SBET N2 values range from 1.352 to 7.277 m2/g, with the highest values for Krosno Beds samples. The mudstones and claystones of the Menilite, Krosno and Grybów beds are primarily affected by compaction, with only a minor influence from cementation and dissolution. The evaluated mudstones do not qualify as effective shale oil/gas source rock; despite good thermal maturity, their hydrocarbon generation potential at the analysed depths is very low. It could be hypothesised that, given the overall volume of nanopores and their interconnectivity, such a potential unconventional hydrocarbon system may occur at greater depths or in regions where hydrocarbon generation potential has been documented, even at shallower depths.

results.title: Harmony by Choice

abstracts.content: This chapter presents a detailed framework for ensuring national cohesion and preserving the unitary character of the proposed decentralized constitutional system. Central to this vision is a set of innovative institutions designed to balance self-governance with harmony. The College of the Voivodships will serve as a hub for coordinating decentralized policymaking and fostering peer review. A National Ranking of Public Services will comprehensively assess the quality of services delivered by local and regional governments, promoting transparency and accountability. Regions with aligned policy goals may establish structured frameworks for Close Cooperation. The popularly elected President of the Republic will hold broad oversight powers to uphold the legality of subnational measures and the constitutionality of their legislation. A strengthened National Health Fund and social security system will maintain their redistributive functions, acting as both societal glue and key pillars of Poland’s national identity.
